idiom_name: hard-private # elements inside the owning class plus the module/package export surface as the grant
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no compile-time access control; what it has is hard runtime privacy in #-prefixed class elements - the encapsulation is 'enforced by JavaScript itself', a reference from outside the declaring class is a syntax error, and unlike TypeScript's private modifier there is no bracket-notation or property-lookup escape (MDN, private elements). The attorney therefore becomes the owning class plus the module boundary: keep the implementation in # members of the class that owns it, hand out the narrow granted surface from a method of that class (a returned object of bound closures is the idiomatic capability form), and export only that surface; for package consumers the package.json exports field encapsulates everything not listed, although a direct absolute-path require still reaches the file.
pitfalls: # privacy is per class, not per file: no function outside the class body can name #recalc, so an attorney for that class has to be produced by the class itself (a method returning bound closures) rather than written beside it.

An underscore prefix is not the mechanism: _recalc stays a perfectly callable own property at runtime, and even TypeScript's compile-time private is reachable through bracket access or plain-JS consumers.

The exports field encapsulates subpaths for importers but is documented as 'not a strong encapsulation' - a direct require of an absolute path inside the package still loads the module - and bundler re-exports can expose more than the entry point suggests.
